newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resid fuel prices mixed, trade thin.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resid fuel prices mixed, trade thin.

text.p: U.S. spot fuel oil prices were narrowly mixed Tuesday in slack trade, with interest for very low sulphur grades raising values slightly, while mid- and high sulphurs were pressured by a lack of utility demand.

"The only demand is for restocking and it's not urgent, but there's not a lot of (0.3 percent) HP around," said one East Coast utility buyer, adding loads lately have slumped from mild weather in the region.
In New York Harbor, 0.3 percent high pour notionally moved up slightly to near the $17 a barrel mark, with delivered barrels talked at $17.25 or higher, traders said.
NYH physical one percent was steady to down slightly at $15.75-16.00, with July one percent paper talked little changed in the $15.55-80 area.
High sulphurs in New York also were unchanged to modestly lower, with 2.2 percent now pegged on either side of $14.50, traders said.
At the U.S. Gulf, prices remained stable, with three percent still quoted at $14.50 and one percent at $16.00.
Traders said Gulf Coast grades, particularly high sulphur, seemed better supported than supply on the East Coast after recent sales to Mexico.

New York city gate gas prices stayed unchanged Tuesday in the low-$2.40s/mmBtu, or $15.31 a barrel equivalent. Gas at Henry Hub, the NYMEX delivery point, also held steady at about $2.19/mmBtu, or $13.80 a barrel.
